habitat: The upper stratum of forests and valley bush.
summary: A fairly common summer resident. The male is bright green from the beak to the tail and on the breast, with a yellow belly, no white on the head, a dark eye and a green beak. The female is brown above and white below with heavy green banding, lacks the white mark behind the eye, and has darker barring, a dark eye and a bluish bill and feet. The call is a clear Pretty, Geor-gie. It parasitises forest robins, warblers and flycatchers. Months were left unset.

similar.note: Female Klaas’s Cuckoo has a white mark behind the eye and finer, darker barring below. The female emerald lacks that white mark and is more bronze above.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^1=2 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 1–4.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: No white mark behind the eye.

upperparts.pattern: Much more bronze on the upper parts than female Klaas’s Cuckoo.

underparts.pattern: Heavily barred below, with heavy green banding.

calls.description: A clear Pretty, Geor-gie. Newman does not say which sex gives it. Grade A from Ithala Game Reserve. The catalogue types it as song and the filename says a male song. It is not a Kruger recording.
